summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted after a syncopal episode while walking without oxygen. He had been unwell for weeks with diarrhea, fatigue, and poor oral intake. Workup revealed Staph epidermidis bacteremia from his PICC line, confirmed by blood and catheter tip cultures. The infected PICC was removed and a new one placed in the right arm. He received daptomycin for a planned three-week course, transitioning from initial vancomycin. Multiple therapeutic paracenteses were performed for symptomatic ascites, with fluid negative for SBP. A TEE showed no endocarditis, and an EGD revealed grade II esophageal varices, which were banded. Cardiology attributed the syncope to hypovolemia and infection rather than arrhythmia, recommending nadolol. His diarrhea was deemed due to remodulin, with infectious causes ruled out. He developed transient renal dysfunction from diuresis, managed by dose reduction. He improved clinically, was stabilized on home oxygen and remodulin, and was discharged on IV daptomycin with close outpatient follow-up.
